title: Java Reference
description: A compact reference of the Java language features and standard library classes covered in the tutorial, grouped by topic, with syntax, a short example and the lesson that explains each one.

entries.name: Primitive types
entries.summary: The eight built-in value types: byte, short, int, long, float, double, char and boolean. Everything else is a reference type.
entries.syntax: int count = 42; long big = 9_000_000_000L; double ratio = 2.5; float f = 2.5f; char c = 'A'; boolean ok = true;
notes: A whole-number literal is an int unless it has the L suffix; a decimal literal is a double unless it has the f suffix.
Integer division truncates: 7 / 2 is 3. int overflow wraps silently.

entries.name: var
entries.summary: Declares a local variable whose type the compiler infers from the initialiser. The variable is still statically typed.
entries.syntax: var name = "Ada"; var items = new ArrayList<String>();
notes: Only for local variables with an initialiser; not for fields, parameters or uninitialised declarations.

entries.name: final
entries.summary: Marks a variable that may be assigned exactly once, a method that cannot be overridden, or a class that cannot be extended.
entries.syntax: final int MAX_RETRIES = 3;
notes: A final reference cannot be re-pointed, but the object it refers to may still change.

entries.name: public static void main
entries.summary: The entry point the JVM calls when a class is run. args holds the command-line arguments.
entries.syntax: public static void main(String[] args) { ... }
notes: Java 25 also accepts a compact form, void main() { IO.println("Hi"); }, in a source file run with java File.java.

entries.name: System.out.println / printf
entries.summary: println prints a value and a line break, print prints without one, and printf fills placeholders such as %s, %d, %.2f and %n.
entries.syntax: System.out.printf("%s is %d years (%.1f%%)%n", name, age, pct);

entries.name: Type casting
entries.summary: Widening conversions (int to long to double) happen automatically; narrowing ones need an explicit cast and may lose data.
entries.syntax: int whole = (int) 9.99;   // 9
notes: A cast from double to int truncates toward zero; use Math.round for rounding.
Casting a large int to byte keeps only the low 8 bits: (byte) 130 is -126.

entries.name: if / else if / else
entries.summary: Runs the first block whose boolean condition is true; the else block runs when none matched.
entries.syntax: if (a > b) { ... } else if (a == b) { ... } else { ... }
notes: The condition must be a boolean; if (count) does not compile. The ternary form cond ? a : b picks one of two values.

entries.name: switch expression
entries.summary: Chooses a value from several cases using arrows; no fall-through, several labels per case, and yield for block bodies.
entries.syntax: String kind = switch (day) { case "SAT", "SUN" -> "weekend"; default -> "weekday"; };
notes: Must be exhaustive: add default unless switching over an enum or sealed type with every case listed.

entries.name: switch statement (classic)
entries.summary: The older colon form: execution continues from the matching label until a break, so a missing break falls through.
entries.syntax: switch (x) { case 1: ...; break; case 2: ...; break; default: ...; }

entries.name: for loop
entries.summary: Repeats with an initialiser, a condition checked before each iteration and an update run after each iteration.
entries.syntax: for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) { ... }

entries.name: Enhanced for loop
entries.summary: Visits every element of an array or collection without an index.
entries.syntax: for (String name : names) { ... }
notes: Do not remove from a collection inside this loop; use removeIf or an Iterator.

entries.name: while / do-while
entries.summary: while repeats as long as a condition is true, checking first; do-while checks after the body, so it runs at least once.
entries.syntax: while (cond) { ... }   do { ... } while (cond);

entries.name: break / continue
entries.summary: break leaves the innermost loop or switch; continue skips to the next iteration.
entries.syntax: if (done) break;   if (skip) continue;
notes: A label (outer:) lets break outer; leave a nested loop in one step.

entries.name: class
entries.summary: Declares a type with fields (state) and methods (behaviour). Objects are created from it with new.
entries.syntax: public class BankAccount { private double balance; public void deposit(double amount) { ... } }
notes: One public class per file, and the file name must match it.

entries.name: Constructor
entries.summary: A method with the class name and no return type that initialises a new object; runs when new is used.
entries.syntax: public BankAccount(String owner, double opening) { this.owner = owner; this.balance = opening; }
notes: If you declare no constructor, Java provides an empty no-argument one; declare any and that default disappears.

entries.name: this
entries.summary: A reference to the current object; needed when a parameter shadows a field and to call another constructor with this(...).
entries.syntax: this.name = name;

entries.name: static
entries.summary: A static field is shared by all instances; a static method belongs to the class and is called without an object.
entries.syntax: private static int count = 0;   public static int issued() { return count; }
notes: Static methods cannot use this or instance fields.

entries.name: Access modifiers
entries.summary: private: this class only; no modifier: the same package; protected: package plus subclasses; public: everywhere.
entries.syntax: private double balance;   protected String name;   public void deposit(double amount)

entries.name: extends / super
entries.summary: extends makes a subclass that inherits the parent's members; super(...) calls the parent constructor and super.method() the parent version.
entries.syntax: class Dog extends Animal { Dog(String name) { super(name); } }
notes: A class can extend only one class.

entries.name: @Override
entries.summary: Marks a method that replaces an inherited one and makes the compiler verify that such a method exists in a supertype.
entries.syntax: @Override public String toString() { ... }
notes: Without the annotation a typo silently creates a new, unrelated method.

entries.name: abstract
entries.summary: An abstract class cannot be instantiated and may declare abstract methods without a body that subclasses must implement.
entries.syntax: abstract class Employee { abstract double monthlyPay(); }

entries.name: interface / implements
entries.summary: A contract of methods a class promises to provide; a class may implement several. default methods carry a body.
entries.syntax: interface Shape { double area(); default String describe() { ... } }   class Circle implements Shape { ... }
notes: Interface methods are public, so implementations must be public too.

entries.name: sealed / permits
entries.summary: Restricts which classes or records may implement an interface or extend a class, so a switch over it can be checked for completeness.
entries.syntax: sealed interface Shape permits Circle, Square {}
notes: Available since Java 17; pairs naturally with records and switch patterns.

entries.name: enum
entries.summary: A type with a fixed set of named constants that may have fields, constructors and methods.
entries.syntax: enum Size { SMALL(250), MEDIUM(350); private final int ml; Size(int ml) { this.ml = ml; } }
notes: Compare enum values with ==; a switch over an enum needs no default when every constant is listed.

entries.name: ArrayList
entries.summary: A resizable list with index access that keeps insertion order and allows duplicates.
entries.syntax: List<String> tasks = new ArrayList<>(); tasks.add("x"); tasks.get(0); tasks.size();
notes: remove(int) removes by index, remove(Object) by value: use remove(Integer.valueOf(1)) for a List<Integer>.
getFirst, getLast and reversed exist since Java 21.

entries.name: List.of / Set.of / Map.of
entries.summary: Create unmodifiable collections in one expression. Adding or removing throws UnsupportedOperationException.
entries.syntax: List<Integer> fixed = List.of(3, 1, 2); Map<String, Integer> m = Map.of("a", 1);
notes: Wrap in new ArrayList<>(...) or new HashMap<>(...) to get a modifiable copy.

entries.name: HashMap / LinkedHashMap / TreeMap
entries.summary: Key-value maps: HashMap is unordered and fastest, LinkedHashMap keeps insertion order, TreeMap sorts by key.
entries.syntax: Map<String, Integer> stock = new HashMap<>(); stock.put("apple", 5); stock.get("apple"); stock.getOrDefault("kiwi", 0);
notes: get returns null for a missing key; getOrDefault avoids the null.

entries.name: HashSet / TreeSet
entries.summary: Sets hold each value once; add returns false for a duplicate. HashSet is unordered, TreeSet sorted, LinkedHashSet in insertion order.
entries.syntax: Set<String> seen = new HashSet<>(); boolean isNew = seen.add("ada");

entries.name: Map.merge
entries.summary: Stores a value for an absent key or combines it with the existing one, which makes counting a one-liner.
entries.syntax: counts.merge(word, 1, Integer::sum);

entries.name: Generic class and method
entries.summary: A type parameter in angle brackets lets a class or method work for any element type while staying type-safe.
entries.syntax: class Box<T> { private T content; }   static <T> T firstOrDefault(List<T> items, T fallback) { ... }
notes: Type arguments must be reference types: List<Integer>, never List<int>.

entries.name: Bounds and wildcards
entries.summary: T extends Comparable<T> restricts a type parameter; ? extends X reads from a list of any subtype, ? super X writes into a list of any supertype.
entries.syntax: static <T extends Comparable<T>> T max(List<T> items)   static double total(List<? extends Number> nums)
notes: Generics are invariant: a List<Integer> is not a List<Number>; wildcards express the safe relationships (PECS: producer extends, consumer super).

entries.name: Common String methods
entries.summary: length, charAt, substring, indexOf, contains, startsWith, toUpperCase, strip, replace, split, join and repeat cover most text work.
entries.syntax: s.length(); s.charAt(0); s.substring(1, 3); s.indexOf("x"); s.split(" "); String.join("-", parts);
notes: Strings are immutable: every method returns a new string and leaves the original unchanged.

entries.name: equals / equalsIgnoreCase / compareTo
entries.summary: Compare string contents with equals; == compares references and is wrong for strings built at run time. compareTo orders strings.
entries.syntax: if (answer.equals("yes"))   "apple".compareTo("banana") < 0
notes: Write "yes".equals(answer) when answer might be null.

entries.name: StringBuilder
entries.summary: A mutable text buffer for building strings efficiently in loops; append, insert, reverse, setLength and toString.
entries.syntax: StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder(); sb.append("a").append(1); String s = sb.toString();

entries.name: Text block
entries.summary: A multi-line string literal between triple quotes; the indentation common to all lines is removed.
notes: Available since Java 15. The closing quotes on their own line add a final newline; place them after the last text to omit it.

entries.name: String.format / formatted
entries.summary: Builds a string from a format template with the same placeholders as printf.
entries.syntax: String.format("%.2f", 3.14159)   "%d%% done".formatted(75)

entries.name: try / catch / finally
entries.summary: Runs the try block, handles a thrown exception in the first matching catch, and always runs finally for cleanup.
entries.syntax: try { ... } catch (NumberFormatException e) { ... } finally { ... }
notes: List specific exceptions before general ones; combine unrelated types with catch (A | B e).

entries.name: throw
entries.summary: Raises an exception object; execution leaves the current statement and unwinds until a handler catches it.
entries.syntax: throw new IllegalArgumentException("price must not be negative");

entries.name: throws
entries.summary: Declares that a method may throw a checked exception, passing the obligation to handle it to the caller.
entries.syntax: void withdraw(double amount) throws InsufficientFundsException { ... }
notes: Unchecked exceptions (RuntimeException and subclasses) need no declaration; checked ones must be caught or declared.

entries.name: try-with-resources
entries.summary: Declares AutoCloseable resources in the try header so they are closed automatically, even when an exception occurs.
entries.syntax: try (BufferedReader reader = Files.newBufferedReader(path)) { ... }

entries.name: Custom exception class
entries.summary: Extend Exception for a checked exception or RuntimeException for an unchecked one, and pass the message to super.
entries.syntax: class InsufficientFundsException extends Exception { InsufficientFundsException(String msg) { super(msg); } }

entries.name: Scanner
entries.summary: Reads typed input from System.in: nextLine for a whole line, nextInt and nextDouble for the next token.
entries.syntax: Scanner in = new Scanner(System.in); String name = in.nextLine(); int age = Integer.parseInt(in.nextLine().strip());
notes: nextInt leaves the newline in the buffer, so a following nextLine returns an empty string; read lines and parse them instead.

entries.name: Files and Path
entries.summary: Static methods for whole-file I/O: writeString, readString, readAllLines and lines, with StandardOpenOption.APPEND to add to a file.
entries.syntax: Path p = Path.of("notes.txt"); Files.writeString(p, text); String all = Files.readString(p); List<String> lines = Files.readAllLines(p);
notes: All of these throw the checked IOException. A relative path is resolved against the folder the program was started from.

entries.name: record
entries.summary: An immutable data class declared from its components; constructor, accessors, equals, hashCode and toString are generated.
entries.syntax: record Point(int x, int y) {}   Point p = new Point(1, 2); p.x();
notes: Components are final; create a new record instead of modifying one. A record may implement interfaces but cannot extend a class.

entries.name: Lambda expression
entries.summary: A short anonymous function passed where a functional interface (Function, Predicate, Comparator, Runnable) is expected.
entries.syntax: n -> n * n   (a, b) -> a + b   s -> s.length() > 5

entries.name: Method reference
entries.summary: A lambda that only calls one existing method, written with :: for brevity.
entries.syntax: Product::name   Integer::sum   String::toUpperCase   TreeMap::new

entries.name: Stream pipeline
entries.summary: Intermediate operations (filter, map, sorted, distinct, limit) describe a transformation; one terminal operation (toList, count, sum, max, forEach) runs it.
entries.syntax: list.stream().filter(p -> p.price() < 10).map(Product::name).toList()
notes: A stream can be consumed once; create a new one from the source for each pipeline.
IntStream.rangeClosed(1, 5) and mapToInt give primitive streams with sum, average, min and max.

entries.name: Collectors
entries.summary: Terminal reductions for collect: toList, toSet, joining, groupingBy, counting and more.
entries.syntax: collect(Collectors.joining(", "))   collect(Collectors.groupingBy(Product::category, Collectors.counting()))

entries.name: Optional
entries.summary: A container that either holds a value or is empty, returned by findFirst, max and min; use orElse, map or ifPresent instead of null checks.
entries.syntax: Optional<Product> top = stream.max(cmp); String name = top.map(Product::name).orElse("none");
